about.title: Emeryville Product Liability Claims
about.longDescription: Emeryville is a small city, but its mix of dense retail centers, warehouses near I-80, and busy residential blocks means defective products show up in daily life here just as often as anywhere else — a malfunctioning kitchen appliance, a faulty e-bike battery, a piece of gym equipment that fails, or a tool used on a job site off Hollis Street or 40th Street. Under California law, injured people generally don't have to prove a manufacturer was careless; strict liability means showing the product itself was defective and that the defect caused harm. That applies whether the defect came from design, manufacturing, or a missing warning. LawProactive doesn't practice law — we're a free connection service that puts you in touch with an independent attorney who can evaluate what happened, help you preserve the product as evidence, and explain who along the supply chain — maker, distributor, or retailer — may share responsibility.

whyChoose.title: Why Emeryville Residents Turn to LawProactive

items.title: Strict Liability Can Simplify Your Path
items.desc: Because California often applies strict liability to defective products, an attorney may focus on the product's condition and the harm it caused rather than trying to prove the manufacturer was careless.

items.title: Multiple Parties May Share Responsibility
items.desc: A defect claim can reach beyond the manufacturer to distributors or retailers who sold the product, giving an attorney more than one avenue to pursue on your behalf.

items.title: Preserving Evidence Matters Early
items.desc: Keeping the defective product, packaging, and any receipts intact can be critical to a claim, and an attorney can advise you on safely storing that evidence right away.

items.question: Do I have to prove the manufacturer was negligent?
items.answer: Not usually. California product liability claims often rely on strict liability, meaning you generally need to show the product was defective and that the defect caused your injury. An independent attorney can walk you through what evidence supports that.

items.question: What should I do with the product that hurt me?
items.answer: Keep it exactly as it was when the injury happened, along with any packaging, instructions, or receipts. Don't attempt repairs or discard anything, since the product itself is often the most important piece of evidence in these claims.

items.question: Are defective product injuries common in a small city like Emeryville?
items.answer: Emeryville's mix of retail centers, warehouses, and busy corridors like I-80 and Powell Street means residents encounter all kinds of consumer and industrial products daily. Local crash data shows 135 injury collisions and 187 people injured in the most recent year, and product-related injuries can occur separately from traffic incidents in homes, stores, and job sites throughout the city.

items.question: Is there a cost to find out if I have a claim?
items.answer: No. LawProactive is a free service that connects you with an independent attorney, and attorneys in the network typically work on contingency, meaning there's no fee unless you recover compensation.
